parachute-drop.name: Parachute Drop Challenge
parachute-drop.desc: Design and test a parachute to minimize impact force
parachute-drop.overview: Record your drop measurements and video analysis below. Please follow all instructions carefully.
parachute-drop.timeUpText: Your 60 minutes are up. The form is now locked, but you can still review your data and use instant calculate.
parachute-drop.equipment: Army figurine, Plastic bag or paper (parachute material), String, Masking tape, Meter ruler or measuring tape, Mobile phone (for slow-mo video recording)
parachute-drop.instruction1: Measure and record the mass of your toy.
parachute-drop.instruction2: Set up a drop zone with a known height.
parachute-drop.instruction4: Record a slow-motion video of the drop.
parachute-drop.instruction5: Use the video playback to measure exact fall time.
parachute-drop.instruction6: Calculate forces or use Instant Calc (with penalty).
parachute-drop.integrityInstruction: Input your manual calculations below. High School teams must provide these calculations.
parachute-drop.formulaSpeedPrimary: Speed (m/s) = Drop Height (m) ÷ Time to Contact (s)
parachute-drop.formulaVelocity: Velocity (m/s) = (2 × Drop Height) ÷ Time to Contact
parachute-drop.calcWarningText: Using the instant calculator will deduct 20 points from your team's score. Continue?
parachute-drop.timerPauseWarning: Only pause the timer if you need to. Keep your data honest!

experiment.round1IntroText: The phone measures movement quietly. Perform each movement slowly for 10 seconds after the countdown.
experiment.round2IntroText: Same movements again. If you are too shaky, the screen turns red with a warning and the phone says "Slow" — so you can adjust even if you cannot feel a buzz.
experiment.currentHint: Watch the screen — red + "Slow" means ease up.
experiment.promptText: Tap Start now. Countdown 3, 2, 1, then Go. Recording lasts 10 seconds — Done plays when finished.
